# Surefire groups for the GitHub Actions Build workflow (build.yml, Linux) and the Windows tests
# workflow (windows-tests.yml), both read through .github/scripts/test-shards.py; the two run
# the whole suite. ci.jenkins.io does not use the groups: its Jenkinsfile is a plain
# buildPlugin call that runs only the @Tag("core") tests (pom.xml, core-tests-on-jenkins).
#
# Format: a group starts with a line "[<label>]"; the lines after it, up to the next
# "[<label>]" line, hold its Surefire -Dtest patterns, separated by commas, spaces or line
# breaks. Lines starting with '#' are comments.
#   label    words of lower-case letters and digits separated by single spaces or '-', at
#            most 25 characters. It names the job, "test (jdk 21, <label>)", so say what
#            the group tests. Its id, the label with '-' for every space ("run-approval"),
#            names the surefire-reports artifact and is the argument of "verify".
#   pattern  matched against the simple class name; only letters, digits, '_' and '*' are
#            allowed. Either a prefix ("Grant*Test") or one class name.
#
# Groups are features, by test class name. Estimates per group, from the per-class times of
# Build runs 38508937576 (main) and 38499172942 (four jobs per class: two runs, JDK 21 and
# 25; ~25,500 s of class time per JDK). The four classes Wave D D2 added (FilterDropdownTest,
# ResultLabelPageTest, StatusLabelPageTest, ui.StatusLabelsTest) had no CI run yet: their
# times are local times scaled by 1.36, the mean ratio of CI to local time of two classes
# timed in the same local run (PageTitleIdRowTest 1.60, DashboardLimitTest 1.12). "s" is the
# group's mean class time; "min" is the job time, mean and slowest of the four samples, from
# a model that hands the group's classes, in the order Surefire runs them (alphabetical by
# class file), to four forks (forkCount 1C on the runner's four cores) and adds ~50 s of
# compilation and job setup. On these runs the model came within 25 s of every measured
# Surefire run of the ten earlier groups.
#   run requests               33 classes  ~2,360 s  11.4 / 12.8 min
#   run approval and mail      28 classes  ~2,310 s  11.5 / 12.9 min
#   activation and new jobs    28 classes  ~2,580 s  12.0 / 13.3 min
#   incidents refusals reruns  21 classes  ~2,300 s  11.6 / 11.8 min
#   permission windows         33 classes  ~2,650 s  12.3 / 13.2 min
#   items and moves            19 classes  ~2,290 s  10.6 / 11.4 min
#   authorization and links    27 classes  ~2,600 s  13.1 / 13.3 min
#   permissions and plugins    40 classes  ~2,160 s  10.7 / 12.0 min
#   audit history and storage  50 classes  ~2,740 s  12.7 / 14.1 min
#   build parameters           19 classes  ~1,800 s   9.8 / 10.6 min
#   pages forms and config     19 classes  ~1,700 s  10.0 / 10.3 min
# ItemIdentityBindingTest (~545 s, items and moves) and AuthorizationEntryGuardTest (~535 s,
# authorization and links) are the two slowest classes; each sorts among the first four
# classes of its group, so it starts at once. The last two groups were one, "parameters and
# ui", until D2: with D2's classes it came out at 16.7 / 17.9 min in the same model, against
# 14.2 min (mean of the four jobs) measured without them.
#
# .github/scripts/test-shards.py check fails the workflow when a test class matches no
# group or more than one group, when a group matches no class and when a pattern matches
# no class (left behind by a rename or a deletion). A new test class whose name starts like
# the classes of one group needs no change here if that group has its prefix; otherwise add
# the prefix or the class name to the group of the feature it tests. Rebalance (move a
# family to another group, or split a feature into two descriptively labelled groups) when
# one group grows much slower than the others.
